 Judgment
Though this appeal is listed for admission, with the consent of both counsel, it is taken up for final disposal.

2. This miscellaneous first appeal is filed by petitioner under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act (for short 'the Act'), seeking enhancement of compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident dated 10.07.2011.
3. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.
4. It is the case of the petitioner that he is a cleaner.

On 10.07.2011 at about 11:00 p.m. petitioner was proceeding towards Sirgeri on Hero Honda motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-01-EN-2536 ('offending vehicle' for short) as a pillion rider, on Genekihal-Kurugod main road.
It was driven by respondent No.1-Nagaraj in rash or negligent manner, as a result of which, he lost control and it turned turtule.

In the said accident, the petitioner sustained grievous injuries resulting in Sri.Santoshkumar vs Sri.Nataraj C.M. And Ors on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181505658/

Despite prolonged treatment, he is not completely cured.
As driver-cum-owner and insurer, respondent Nos.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

During the pendency of the petition, petitioner impleded respondent No.3. have remained ex parte.
6.

Respondent No.2 has filed written statement disputing that accident occurred due to rash or negligent driving of offending vehicle, the age, occupation, income of the petitioner, nature of the injuries sustained by him and that they have resulted in permanent partial disability and also incurred medical expenses for the treatment.
Petitioner sustained injuries due to fall and prays to dismiss the petition.
7. Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.

8. Petitioner got himself examined as P.W.1 and the doctor as P.W.2 and relied upon Exs.P1 to 14.
9.
On behalf of respondent No.2 one witness examined as RW.1 and Ex.D1 is marked.

10. Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition filed by the petitioner granting compensation in a sum of Rs.6,29,658/- with interest at 6% per annum and directed respondent No.2 to pay the same as detailed below:

sentences.text: During the course of arguments, learned counsel representing the petitioner submitted that the income taken by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
The compensation granted under all the heads required reconsideration and prays to allow the appeal.
13. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.2 supported the impugned judgment and award and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

14. Heard arguments and perused the records.
15.
Having regard to the fact that the respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award

, the findings of the Tribunal that the accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle and in the said accident, the petitioner sustained injuries has attained finality.
16. Based on the record, the Tribunal has correctly taken the age of petitioner as 22 years and applied 18 multiplier is correct.

Though petitioner has claimed that he was earning Rs.10,000/- per month, in the absence of convincing evidence the Tribunal has considered income as Rs.9000/-,
which is fairly higher than the notional income based on minimum wages for the year 2011.

Similarly, considering the medical evidence, the Tribunal has rightly taken the disability at 13% and therefore, the compensation granted in a sum of Rs.2,52,720/- under the head loss of future income due disability is just and reasonable and it requires no interference.

17. Based on medical bills the Tribunal has rightly granted compensation in a sum of Rs.2,77,938/-
and it also calls for no interference.

At the rate of Rs.9,000/- per month for a period of three months the Tribunal has correctly granted compensation in a sum of Rs.27,000/- under the loss of income during laid up period and there is no scope for interference.
The compensation granted in a sum of Rs.22,000/- under the head attendant charges, food nourishment and conveyance is on the lower side and the same is enhanced to Rs.30,000/-.

18. Having regard to the nature of injuries suffered which has resulted in disability and the year of accident compensation granted in a sum of Rs.40,000/- under the head pain & suffering is just and reasonable.
However, Rs.10,000/- granted under the head loss of amenities is enhanced to Rs.20,000/-.

19. Thus, in all the petitioner is entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.6,47,658/- and same is rounded of to Rs.6,50,000/- together with interest at 6% p.a., as against Rs.6,29,658/- granted by the Tribunal as detailed below:

Of course as the insurer of the offending vehicle, respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation with accrued interest.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (i) The Appeal is allowed in part.

(ii) The appellant is entitled for compensation in a sum of Rs.6,47,658/- and same is rounded of to Rs.6,50,000/- together with interest at 6% p.a. as against Rs.6,29,658/- .
(iii) Respondent No.2/Insurance company shall deposit the compensation amount together with interest at 6% p.a. within a period of six weeks from the date of this order (Minus the compensation already paid/deposited).
(iv) Vide order dated 21.11.2019, the petitioner is not entitled to interest for delay of 261 days on the enhanced compensation.
- 10 - (v) Registry is directed to send a copy of this order to the Tribunal.
